parsed_proposal.diagnosis: The issue is that AbortSignal listeners are not being properly cleaned up after tasks complete. The current implementation adds a listener in #throwOnAbort but doesn't remove it when the task finishes successfully, is rejected, times out, or is aborted. This causes memory leaks when using shared AbortSignals.
parsed_proposal.hypothesis: We need to ensure that AbortSignal listeners are removed in all code paths - successful completion, rejection, timeout, and abortion - by storing the listener reference and calling removeEventListener appropriately.
parsed_proposal.reason: The current #throwOnAbort method creates a one-time listener but doesn't provide a mechanism to clean it up when the task completes through other means. This leads to accumulating listeners on shared AbortSignals.
